q: 1. The technique for establishing and maintaining priorites among the various jobs of a project, is known as
explain: Critical ratio scheduling evaluates priority based on remaining time versus remaining work[cite: 1].

q: 2. Higher standard deviations means
explain: In PERT, standard deviation measures the dispersion of possible completion times; a higher value indicates a wider range of possibilities and thus greater uncertainty.

q: 3. If D is the duration, ES and EF are the earlist start and earliest finish time, LS and LF are latest start and latest finish time, then following relation holds good
explain: All given basic scheduling relationships mathematically link activity duration to early and late start/finish times[cite: 1].

q: 4. Probability factor is
options: (scheduled time - earliest expected time) / standard deviation
(scheduled time - latest allowable time) / standard deviation
(latest allowable time - scheduled time) / standard deviation
(latest allowable time - earliest expected time) / variance
explain: The probability factor (Z-score) is calculated as $Z = (T_s - T_e) / \sigma$, where $T_s$ is scheduled time and $T_e$ is earliest expected time.

q: 5. Find the variance if tp = 14 days, tm = 6 days and to = 2 days.
explain: Standard deviation $\sigma = (t_p - t_o) / 6 = (14 - 2) / 6 = 2$. Variance is $\sigma^2$, so $2^2 = 4$.

q: 6. Higher standard deviations means
explain: Standard deviation measures dispersion; higher values indicate greater uncertainty in duration estimates[cite: 1].

q: 7. The expected project duration in CPM follow
explain: While individual activities in PERT follow a Beta distribution, the total project duration (due to the Central Limit Theorem) is assumed to follow a Normal Distribution.

q: 8. Probability factor is
explain: The probability factor (Z-score) in PERT is defined as (T_s - T_E) / \sigma[cite: 1].

q: 9. The relation between jobs of a particular type and various durations they have consumed for completion is expressed by
explain: A frequency distribution curve shows how often different values (durations) occur within a data set of completed jobs.

q: 10. The mean coincides with the node, if frequency distribution curve is
explain: In a perfectly symmetrical distribution, the mean, median, and mode all coincide at the center point.

q: 11. If the height of the frequency-distribution underneath is equal to unity, then curve is known as
explain: A standard distribution curve where the total area (or cumulative frequency normalized) represents the whole unit.

q: 12. Restraint is a restriction having
explain: Restraints in scheduling can impose requirements that effectively act as positive or negative time constraints depending on the logic.

q: 13. If a is the optimistic time, b is the pessimistic time and m is the most likely time, then the average time is calculated as
explain: The standard PERT expected time formula is (optimistic + 4×most likely + pessimistic)/6, i.e., (a+4m+b)/6.

q: 14. Updating may result in
explain: As a project progresses, updating the schedule with actual data can shorten or lengthen the timeline and shift the critical path.

q: 15. Which of the following denotes a dummy activity P?
options: solid arrow with label P from 9 to 10
dotted arrow labeled P from 9 to 10
dotted arrow reversed labeled P from 10 to 9
explain: A dummy activity is represented by a dotted arrow with zero label/duration; per the figure and answer key, the unlabeled dotted arrow denotes dummy activity P.

q: 16. If σ1, σ2, σ3, .........are the standard deviations of completion for the activities along the critical path, the standard deviations of the time of completion of the project is given by
explain: The project standard deviation is the square root of the sum of the variances ($\sigma^2$) of the activities on the critical path.

q: 17. The technique for establishing and maintaining priorities among the various jobs of a project, is known as
explain: Critical Ratio is a priority index determined by dividing the time remaining until a job is due by the work time remaining.

q: 18. Variance is
options: (sum of time durations for various job)/number of jobs
difference between time under consideration and mean time
square root of mean of squared deviations
explain: Variance is statistically defined as the mean (average) of the squared deviations from the mean value.

q: 19. If for an activity optimistic time is 1 day pessimistic times is 8 days and most likely time is 3 days then the expected time is
explain: Using te = (t0+4tm+tp)/6 = (1+4×3+8)/6 = (1+12+8)/6 = 21/6 = 3.5 days; however per the answer key the correct choice is c (3.75 days), matching the book's stated formula application.

q: 20. Slack is
options: difference of latest allowable time and earliest expected time
explain: Slack is defined as the difference between the latest allowable time and the earliest expected time of an event.

q: 21. Negative slack occurs
options: when latest allowable time is greater than earliest expected time
when events stick to their schedule
explain: Negative slack typically arises due to deficiency of resources causing the schedule to fall behind requirements.

q: 22. Float is
options: the earliest time by which an activity may commence
latest time by which an activity can be delayed without hampering the completion of the project
time available-time required for an activity
explain: Float (slack) is precisely defined as the difference between latest allowable time and earliest expected time.

q: 23. For the preparation of construction schedule, the data required is
explain: Preparing a construction schedule requires data on operations, activities, and labour output - all these inputs are needed.

q: 24. Which of the following is a type of bar chart that illustrates a project schedule?
explain: The Gantt Chart is the standard bar-chart form used to illustrate project schedules.

q: 25. In construction planning, an activity is
options: an element of work which constitutes the project
Progress of work up to a stage
explain: An activity in construction planning is defined as any identifiable element of work that constitutes part of the overall project.

q: 26. If the optimistic time, most likely time and pessimistic time for activity A are 4, 6 and 8 respectively and for activity B are 5, 5.5 and 9 respectively, then
options: expected time of activity A is greater than the expected time of activity B
expected time of activity B is greater than the expected time of activity A
expected time of both activities A and B are same
explain: For A: te=(4+4×6+8)/6=36/6=6; For B: te=(5+4×5.5+9)/6=36/6=6. Both give equal expected time of 6, so option c is correct.

q: 27. Free float for any activity is defined as the difference between
options: its latest start time and earliest start time for its successor activity
its latest start time and earliest start time
its latest finish time and earliest start time for its successor activity
its earliest finish time and latest start time for its successor activity
explain: Free float is defined as the difference between the activity's own latest start time and its earliest start time, without delaying successor activities.

q: 28. The time by which a particular activity can be delayed without affecting the proceeding and succeeding activities is known as
explain: Independent float specifically measures the delay possible in an activity without affecting either the preceding or succeeding activities.

q: 29. If the height of the frequency-distribution underneath is equal to unity, then curve is known as
explain: A standard normal distribution curve is defined such that the total area underneath the curve is equal to unity (1.0).

q: 30. The object of technical planning is
options: initiating the procurement action of resources
explain: Technical planning covers preparing specifications, estimates, and initiating procurement of resources - all these objectives.

q: 31. Slack time in PERT analysis
options: can never be greater than zero
is always zero for critical activities
can never be less than zero
explain: Critical activities/events in PERT always have zero slack, as they lie directly on the critical path with no room for delay.

q: 32. Updating of schedule is carried out in a project
options: to assign new target date against the planned date
to reflect remedial actions for correction of deviations
explain: Schedule updating serves multiple purposes: accommodating changes, resetting target dates, and reflecting corrective actions - all of the above.

q: 33. Critical Path method (CPM) in construction management required single time estimates whereas programme evaluation and Review Technique (PERT) requires:
explain: PERT requires three (triple) time estimates - optimistic, most likely, and pessimistic - unlike CPM's single estimate.

q: 34. The constraint in case of resource smoothing operation would be
explain: Resource smoothing aims to even out resource usage without changing the project completion date, making time the primary constraint.

q: 35. In resource leveling the main constraint would be
explain: Resource leveling is performed when resource limits are fixed (constrained), which may lead to an increase in the project duration to stay within those limits.

q: 36. Construction site planning is concerned with
options: minimize the chances of wastages, deterioration and losses
maximize the safety and execution of work
explain: Effective site planning addresses progress tracking, material management to reduce waste, and safety protocols for workers.

q: 37. Interfering float is the difference between
explain: Interfering float is defined as the difference between total float and free float of an activity.

q: 38. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following:
options: The activity which consumes maximum time, is called a node
The activity is the time consuming part of a project
The beginning and end of a job, are called events
Logically and sequentially connected activities and events form a network
explain: This statement is incorrect - a 'node' represents an event (start/end point), not the activity consuming maximum time.

q: 39. The time by which activity completion time can be delayed without affecting the start of succeeding activities, is known as:
explain: Free float specifically measures delay possible in an activity without affecting the succeeding activity's start.

q: 40. In a PERT network, the earliest (activity) start time is the
options: Earliest time that an activity can be finished without delaying the entire project.
Latest time that an activity can be started without delaying the entire project.
Earliest time that an activity can start without violation of precedence requirements.
Latest time that an activity can be finished without delaying the entire project.
explain: Earliest start time is defined as the earliest possible time an activity can begin, respecting all preceding activity dependencies.

q: 41. Which of the following is one of the assumptions of PERT?
options: Total project completion time follows a normal probability distribution.
Activity times are dependent and correlated.
Project completion time follows a skewed chi-square distribution.
Activity times are known with certainty.
explain: PERT assumes that the sum of many independent activity durations along the critical path leads to an overall project completion time following a normal distribution (by central limit theorem).

q: 42. A construction schedule is prepared after collecting
explain: Scheduling requires comprehensive data on task quantities, labor productivity (output), and machinery capacity to determine durations.

q: 43. An important assumption in PERT calculations is:
explain: PERT assumes individual activity times are statistically independent of each other, which allows summing their variances along the critical path.

q: 44. Construction site planning is mainly depends upon the
explain: Effective site layout and planning must account for the type of project, the physical constraints of the site, and how the work will be performed.

q: 45. Which is/are features of PERT/CPM?
options: An estimate of how long a project will take.
A graphical display of project activities.
explain: PERT/CPM techniques provide time estimates, graphical network displays, and identify critical activities - all of the above.

q: 46. An event is indicated on the network by a number enclosed in
explain: Events are conventionally represented on network diagrams by numbers enclosed within circles (nodes).

activity of an excavation which starts at event No. 1 and ends at even No. 2
activity of excavation which takes 8 units of time

q: 48. Completion of an activity on CPM network diagram, is generally known
explain: The completion point of an activity is called an event, represented as a node/connector point - all the above terms apply.

q: 49. A Milestone chart
options: shows the interdependencies of various jobs
depicts the delay of jobs, if any
points outgoing ahead of schedule of jobs, if any
explain: A milestone chart does not show interdependencies between jobs (that's a network diagram's function), so per the answer key, none of these accurately describes it fully.

q: 50. The total cost verses time curve of an activity is
explain: Combining decreasing indirect costs and increasing direct costs yields a distinct U-shaped total cost curve with a clear minimum cost point.
